probe: resident browser: does the Onshape login survive an MCP child restart, and can the child SEE that it did (issue #6)

environment.host: native Windows, Edge channel msedge, deployment tree C:\MCP\onshapescript
environment.deployed_after: consumer artifact 1.3.0-c10a235, deployed in place (code only), then restarted
environment.bridge: win-wsl-mcp-bridge id=onshape, mode=shared, 6 activeClients; ownedGeneration 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 across the runs below
environment.quota: 0 Onshape REST calls; every step is browser/loopback only

question: Issue #6 accepted two alternatives, the first being: set browser.resident = true, then prove on the real machine that login -> detach -> a NEW MCP child -> action=health reports ok WITHOUT a second human sign-in.
findings_before: The switch was already on: the host's browser.local.toml carries resident = true, and the deployed settings.py merges it (mtime-fresh), so residency was armed but had never actually been exercised.
No browser held the MCP profile and nothing listened on 9333 (Windows process table), i.e. the resident browser did not exist yet.
The deployed build had no detach action, so the literal acceptance sequence could not run on it; the repository HEAD (and the release artifact) do.

timeline.step: 1. spawn the resident browser via login
timeline.result: sessionStatus=awaiting_login; a detached Edge appeared as root PID 10368 with '--remote-debugging-port=9333', '--user-data-dir=...onshape_profile' and NO '--remote-debugging-pipe'; /json/version answered with webSocketDebuggerUrl ws://127.0.0.1:9333/devtools/browser/57634b4c-b117-4245-9174-63d13c83fbfd
timeline.why_it_matters: the driver-owned pipe route (which reaps the browser on driver exit) is not in play; this browser is owned by its own detached process

timeline.tool: human in the visible Edge window, then browser_session action=status

timeline.step: 3. restart the MCP child (no code change yet)
timeline.result: generation 1 -> 2, stoppedGeneration 1, startedGeneration 2, preservedClients 6, force-kill not needed; python children 34576/22860 replaced by 36076/34912
timeline.browser_after: PID 10368 still present, CreationDate unchanged 0:09:26, DevTools GUID unchanged 57634b4c-... ; exactly ONE onshape-profile root process (a new child ATTACHED, it did not launch a second browser)

timeline.step: 4. the new child attaches and reports the login
timeline.result: already logged in (restored Onshape page was kept); status loginConfirmed=true, humanActionRequired=false, same document URL as before the restart
timeline.conclusion: login survives an MCP child restart with zero extra human logins

timeline.step: 5. deploy the repository HEAD artifact (1.3.0-1f9f7c2) in place
timeline.tool: rsync code-only refresh with an allow-list guard, then bridge restart
timeline.result: 27 files written (25 updated + docs/operations/RELEASE.md + RELEASE-NOTES.md), 0 deletions, 397/397 content equality afterwards, 93 host-only development-plane files preserved; excluded state files kept their original 2026 mtimes (a file from the reproducible archive carries 1980-01-01), and the host geometry backend still read enabled:true / cadquery-ocp-wsl
timeline.browser_after_refresh: the resident browser was never touched: it survived a code replacement as well

timeline.step: 6. detach, then a fresh child again
timeline.tool: browser_session action=detach, bridge_control restart, browser_session action=status/health
timeline.result: detach returned detached=true, supported=true, keepBrowser=true, contextClosed=false, browserLeftRunning=true, profileReleased=true, playwrightStopped=true, loginStateMayNeedRefresh=false, previousPageUrl = the same Part Studio; externally PID 10368 and GUID 57634b4c-... unchanged; the next generation's login call answered alreadyAuthenticated=true / needsHumanLogin=false

timeline.tool: browser_session action=health on a fresh child
timeline.result: ok=false: verdict=browser_not_running with note 'No browser resources are held by this MCP process. This probe did NOT launch one, so nothing about the page is known.' -- while the browser was demonstrably alive and still logged in
timeline.why_it_matters: in resident mode 'this process holds nothing' is the NORMAL post-restart state, so that verdict claimed more than the evidence supported; it is also exactly where the owner's acceptance sentence would have failed

timeline.tool: commit c10a235 (health.py/session.py/server.py + 11 tests + docs), artifact rebuilt, 8 files deployed in place, restart generation 4 -> 5
timeline.result: health and status now read the detached browser's own loopback DevTools endpoint (one bounded GET /json/list; no Playwright, no launch, no attach, no page evaluate, no navigation) when, and only when, this process holds no page

verdict=ok; note names the loopback endpoint and the same Part Studio URL and states the page itself was not read; residentBrowser={observed:true, endpoint:http://127.0.0.1:9333, source:devtools-http, pageTargets:1, pageUrl:<same document URL>, onOnshapeApp:true, onSigninPage:false}; sessionStatus=uninitialized, pages=[], probe.responded=null (this process still owns nothing), launchedBrowser=false
timeline.corroboration: action=status on the same child: verdict=ok with the same residentBrowser block while sessionStatus=uninitialized/pageUrl=null/pages=[] kept saying this process holds nothing; action=login then returned alreadyAuthenticated=true / needsHumanLogin=false

timeline.result: PID 10368 (CreationDate 0:09:26) and GUID 57634b4c-b117-4245-9174-63d13c83fbfd unchanged after 1 code refresh, 3 MCP-child restarts and 1 detach

verdict: Issue #6's first alternative is satisfied on the real machine: with browser.resident = true the Onshape login survives an MCP child restart with no second human sign-in, detach succeeds without closing the window, and a fresh child can now REPORT that state (health/status -> ok) instead of claiming no browser exists.
limits: The loopback read proves the browser process answers and which page target it lists. It does NOT prove the page is rendered or that Onshape's server-side session has not expired; the caller's next real call establishes that.
Endpoint-only evidence is labelled as such: probe.responded stays null and the note says the page was not read, so 'ok' here is narrower than a held-page 'ok'.
With resident = false nothing changed: the probe reports browser_not_running exactly as before, because no browser is observable.
A held page is direct evidence and always outranks the endpoint observation.
The detach leg was measured on an attached resident session once; the structural refusal outside resident mode is unchanged and separately pinned by tests.
